inputs.original_text: Cuba seems to be heading toward some kind of political transition. Some Cubans worry that residents own nothing and are too impoverished to take over the few businesses still operating on the island, while the large, wealthy diaspora—and potentially foreign investors—could swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices.
inputs.modified_text: This talk of Cuba “heading toward” a transition sounds less like concern for ordinary people and more like setting the stage for a managed sell-off. If residents own nothing and are too impoverished to buy the businesses still operating, that isn’t just an unfortunate side effect—it leaves them unable to compete while wealthy outsiders wait for bargain prices. The language of transition may be preparing people to accept a transfer of property away from Cubans and into the hands of the diaspora and foreign investors.
